lesson: Listen to where this one starts. Not with you waking, not with a thought, but with a mug on the sill and its ring of cold coffee left overnight. That's a choice. It enters on an object, something small and already there, and lets the room speak before you do. Watch how the image is hand-off. The forgotten mug tells you nothing moves here, then the J lifts off, then the floorboards know your weight, then the cold kettle, the hungry stove. Each one passing the feeling along. Quiet building on quiet. The turn comes when the light leans in, patient as a friend who came early. That's where the picture stops being a picture and becomes a kind of love. Here's the thing to steal. Let one plain object carry the whole mood. The coffee ring does more than any statement could, and notice what those last two lines are doing. I'll let you find that.
